description:
# Concurrent and durable workflow design

2026-10-14. The operator selects concurrent and durable workflows and requests a
deep study of existing Blackbird machinery, fresh frumentarii research, and a
robust design that actively seeks to transcend coding-agent workflow offerings.
Performance tuning is required work. This wave branches away from instrumentation;
existing bugs and required performance work join implementation closeout rather
than becoming prerequisites to this research/design delivery.

## Delivery

Produce a source inventory, fresh coding-agent and durable-workflow studies, a
behavioral comparison matrix, a complete proposed C++/Lua design, direct fault
oracles, and a dependency-aware delivery sequence. Seek capabilities competitors
do not compose, with concrete demonstrations and explicit semantic boundaries.
Do not claim measured superiority from a design or completeness over every
unexamined product. No product implementation, library adoption, provider/eval
traffic, mutation, instrumentation campaign, main integration, or executable
activation is authorized by this design request.

## Source and ownership

Source base 64d75fb on work/workflow-design-2026-10-14, descended from the unmerged
qualification/report branch. Preserve that ancestry; this does not merge its
repairs into master. Preserve operator art, historical worktrees, and stash.
Root owns synthesis/design, common manifest/journal, issue record, document
checks and publication. Three independent conceptual research owners:

- agent_workflows: current coding-agent teams, workflow and intervention semantics.
- durable_workflows: durable execution, structured concurrency, events/schedules,
  data/build lineage and effects.
- native_inventory: actual Blackbird ownership, persistence, Lua and native seams.

All intermediate reports go in this directory. References remain study-only;
archives stay intact on the shared quarantine shelf, extracted copies omit Git
metadata and filesystem detritus, and exact acquisition/restoration is recorded.
Archived instructions have no current authority. Use existing corpora before
acquiring replacements, and note genuinely unavailable material for acquisition.

## Questions the design must answer

1. What runs concurrently, who owns each VM/child, and which execution remains
   available when an operator turn returns or the terminal disconnects?
2. What survives controller/process failure, and what becomes uncertain? How do
   stable decisions, attempts, child outcomes and segment state commit together?
3. How do joins/races, nested resource limits, cancellation, detached work and
   unknown remote effects interact without false completion or deadlock?
4. How can models author and change programs, contexts, execution graphs,
   participants and experiments during ordinary work with coherent activation?
5. How do events, durable waits/schedules, dataflow/statecharts and artifact reuse
   share machinery without erasing their distinct semantics?
6. How do external providers, services, SSH executors and future E2EE peers fit
   without Blackbird governing shared computation or inventing exactly-once effects?
7. What actual hot-path work, copies, wakeups, I/O and recovery complexity must be
   measured, and which direct oracle proves each promised behavior?

## Review and resource use

Three research lanes plus root; no native build/test/profiling jobs. Independent
web/source/library reads can proceed concurrently; archive acquisition is bounded
by source questions and existing material. Design review attacks concrete
concurrency, durable effects/versioning, and model/product expressiveness.
Layer one: one independent attack per conceptual fault family and root repairs.
Layer two: one finding-focused recheck and repairs. No third assurance layer,
review of reviews, revived campaign timers, or repeated historical qualification.
Documentation/link/diff checks and supported Beads backup are the appropriate
checks for this delivery; source test gates remain for future implementation.

## Results

Research, synthesis, review resolutions and final source/publication state will
be linked here when complete. Workflow implementation remains a subsequent
operator discussion over the concrete proposed design.

# Native concurrent workflow implementation

2026-10-15. Operator authorizes implementation with “now send it”. Work only in
`/Users/patrickbeam/projects/blackbird-workflows`, branch
`work/concurrent-durable-workflows-2026-10-15`; the main checkout belongs to a
colleague. The reviewed [design](../../docs/CONCURRENT_DURABLE_WORKFLOWS.md) and
[delivery sequence](../../docs/WORKFLOW_DELIVERY.md) remain the destination.

## First integrated execution path

Build the sole-owner native workflow service and attachable binary client over
the existing RetainedState/AuditLog. Add typed atomic application cells, a bounded
leaf executor and structured join reducer as independent conceptual components.
Compose them into an actual owner process: submit source-pinned native tasks,
execute independent tasks concurrently, preserve exact outcomes, select/commit
joins, cancel explicitly and reopen without replaying released effects.

Use one native semantic ledger. A cell transaction can append native
Decision/Invocation/Admission or terminal Observation events atomically with
state. Existing dispatch opens an attempt before executor visibility; successful
adapter receipt means native scheduling acceptance, never business success.
The final completion and original result update the same task atomically.
Recovery preserves logical command identity and reports released uncertainty;
recovered attempts never become live. Proven-unreleased successor attempts require
the exact recorded evidence and fresh guards specified by the design.

The execution host owns its journal lock, raw-storage grant and service socket.
Clients transfer native BBM2 requests/results; JSON parsing/formatting exists only
at explicitly selected CLI interchange boundaries. Disconnecting every client
does not cancel the host or work. A second owner must fail before task dispatch.
The host polls sockets and a completion wake pipe, without busy inference/timers.
Requests are bounded and partially transferred frames are not commands until
complete. Local private endpoints do not claim E2EE or cross-host takeover.

## Ownership lanes

- Root owns the service/host, CLI, native record integration, CMake, shared
  journal, Beads, build writers, qualification and integration.
- Native inventory lane owns WorkflowStore: typed cells/read sets, exact
  submission idempotency, native event batches, replay and commit/publication.
- Agent workflow lane owns WorkflowExecutor: bounded leaf workers, preallocated
  completion capacity, cancellation observations and owner drain/shutdown.
- Durable workflow lane owns WorkflowJoin: precise modes, member/clock/order
  semantics, immutable selection proposals and acceptance after commit.

Each lane writes its concrete subplan before code, direct tests before source,
and returns its whole conceptual unit. No lane shares a root build/index writer.
Root reviews their API/source before integration. The existing research reviewers
are reused for one concrete code attack and one finding-focused recheck; never
a third layer or review-of-review. Cross-component invariants remain root-owned.

## Direct checks

Independently gate native workers to count real concurrency and aggregate limits.
Reject wrong-owner/reentrant controls, stale revisions/handles and changed-payload
submission identities. Force failed retention before readiness; count zero effects.
Check multi-cell atomicity and native event linkage through actual reopen.
Keep completion bytes when owner publication fails; cancellation records whether
invocation was prevented or only requested. No generic failure implies nonexecution.

Control join completion order/clock and compare exact selected member IDs against
the declared mode; proposals remain unexposed until committed, then immutable.
Exercise unknown outcomes, impossible closed quorum and open-membership closure.
Actual host processes/clients prove detach, sole ownership, exact results and
zero automatic effect replay after SIGKILL. Add direct crash cuts at native
decision/admission/open/result and compare external marker files with retained IDs.

## Resource and verification scope

Use existing C++20/Lua5.4.8 profiles and owned native/BBM2 machinery; no new library.
Only root runs native builds, initially two compiler workers and one Ninja writer
in each owned buildtree. All runtime fixtures use private temporary sessions and
no provider/account requests. Checks: direct debug/release and sanitizer cases
appropriate to changed ownership/lifetime, full installed debug/source gate before
source commits, and scoped Neuroses qualification when the integrated path exists.
No mutation campaign or old instrumentation campaign. Required performance work
measures complete useful native tasks/joins/reopen/capture, retaining all samples;
no invented speed or readiness claims. Existing bugs/tuning join affected closeout.

The wider F5–F12 tool-using model facades, recorded Lua, events/time/streams,
artifacts/demand, live revisions, paradigms and station/remote surfaces follow
their dependencies. Track actual delivery rather than relabeling a native
executor library as the entire programmable workflow system.

# Registered Responses providers and Paper Instruments

The operator requests an isolated worktree and enough configuration to run the
main coding harness with Paper Instruments. Worktree: blackbird-paper-provider;
branch: work/paper-provider-2026-10-15, based on d987f6f. The original checkout's
active TUI changes remain there. No new library or runtime.

## Source contract

Read 2026-10-15: https://docs.paperinstruments.com/docs/ultramarine/responses
and https://docs.paperinstruments.com/docs/ultramarine/chat-completions .
Paper offers https://api.paperinstruments.com/v1/responses and model
ultramarine-1-flash; supports streamed stateless full-history requests and local
function tools. Effort is low/high/max. Developer messages and encrypted reasoning
are unsupported. Plaintext reasoning may be replayed. Function results are strings.
A completed terminal response is required before executing a tool.

## Design and implementation

Keep owned ProviderAuth registrations, account pinning and native external
encoding. Extend the existing registration's protocol choice with
responses-portable: Responses using system instead of developer messages,
plaintext reasoning, and low/high/max effort. This is explicit configuration,
not hostname sniffing or an automatic credential/model fallback. Standard
responses preserves OpenAI fields. Chat/Messages registrations remain colleagues
only. The main selector accepts registered Responses IDs; OpenAI and OpenRouter
keep their existing specialized adapters. Custom providers do not claim support
for the explicit OpenAI/OpenRouter cache policies.

Use a new small RegisteredResponsesCodingProvider with the existing ProviderAuth
transport and completed_response parser. Normalize only the configured portable
request view at the external boundary; retain native context and exact wire
originals through the existing capture. Replace developer roles with system,
omit the encrypted-reasoning include request, and refuse encrypted history rather
than silently deleting it. Preserve plaintext reasoning and call/result identities.
Validate terminal error and completed tool statuses/unique call IDs before dispatch.
Keep account binding pinned across retries; do not follow redirects. No static
key, .env content, or credential enters tracked files, argv or reviewer prompts.

Allow effort max throughout session/program validation, persist the actual custom
provider and effort through reopen/restart/new, and keep OpenRouter's model shape
rule. Validate provider IDs with the same owned identifier alphabet and length.
Add BLACKBIRD_RESPONSES_CURL as the explicit local transport injection for native
protocol checks; normal runs use system curl.

## Direct checks and bound

One remediation layer: meaningful red/green export/transport tests and a native
fake-curl loop requiring exact tool arguments/results and preserved plaintext
reasoning; account-change refusal, invalid provider/protocol, effort max and
session reopen, incomplete/failed/malformed responses must not execute tools.
One independent code challenge and fixes constitute the recheck. Run the required
source gate before committing. No third assurance campaign or unrelated TUI repair.
Build an isolated optimized executable and run a small live Paper tool read plus
follow-up through the actual harness. Read only paper_api_key from workspace .env
without sourcing it; feed auth privately or pass it in the child environment.
Retain logs under ignored context and report actual API restrictions/failures.
Publish the candidate branch; do not merge or activate another checkout.
